# Part III: Operation, Evaluation, and Responsibility {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
Part III executes the complete design loop, establishes design transfer patterns, evaluates AI-assisted workflows against matched baselines, and defines cross-layer architect ownership.
:::

## Part Objectives

- Execute end-to-end design loops that evaluate spatial accelerators across all 8 prompt stack layers.
- Formulate LogCA offload bounds, requalification contracts, and selective classification math to govern design transfer.
- Evaluate AI-assisted methodologies against matched target-only baselines while red-teaming hardware workflows.
- Preserve human architectural commitment authority across silicon tapeout transitions and NRE ROI gatekeeping.

## Part Map

- **@sec-running-the-loop (Running the Design Loop):** Demonstrates an executed study evaluating systolic tensor array candidates against SCALE-Sim and Ramulator memory models.
- **@sec-loop-patterns-across-stack (What Generalizes Across Design Problems):** Establishes LogCA offload bounds, requalification contracts, and Triton-to-RVV 1.0 lowering paths.
- **@sec-evaluating-agentic-architect (Evaluating and Red-Teaming AI-Assisted Systems):** Evaluates AI workflow quality, cost-quality Pareto frontiers, and red-teaming defenses.
- **@sec-what-architect-owns (The Architect's Role):** Analyzes cross-layer responsibility, NRE tapeout ROI gatekeeping, and the field-level outlook.

## Guiding Questions

1. Under what conditions does an architectural candidate or simulator result transfer safely to a new technology context without causing negative transfer?
2. How do we ensure human architects retain exclusive commitment authority over silicon capital and baseline contracts in an era of automated synthesis?
